
=================================================================
#4 Prince Euija  (632)
Arc: Part I — The Three Kingdoms / The King for All · place: sabi · tone: palace coming-of-age
Logline: Thirty-two is late to be named crown prince. By then the clans have had years to decide which of his sons they own.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ In five days, Prince Euija becomes Crown Prince Euija. He is thirty-two, which is late for it. He has fifteen sons, which is early for everything else.
[1] [MAP 632: ]
[2] [CARD King Euija: Righteous and merciful. His father chose it. The son will spend his life deciding which half to keep.]
[3] The Herald: Fifteen, they say. Sixteen by spring. / His Majesty had fifty at that age. They say Samsin keeps a night shift just for Sabi — don’t repeat that.
[4] ¶ This is said admiringly. It is that kind of court.
[5] [PLACE sabi: The king lives here. So do eight families who think that’s a detail.]
[6] ── SCENE: The Rear Garden ──
[7] ¶ At mid-morning the prince is in the rear garden with a bow, a go board, a jar of wine and two court ladies, and he is winning at all four.
[8] ¶ The arrow goes in without his looking. He is already reaching for a stone.
[9] [CITE Prince Euija (32)]
[10] King Euija: Your move. / And if you shift my stone while I drink, my lady, do it better than last time. If I’m to be cheated, I want a professional. Ha! / Pour.
[11] The Court Maids: Your Highness moved it yourself— / —twice— / —and blamed the wind.
[12] [CITE 👑 King Mu (71)]
[13] ¶ The ladies stop giggling all at once, the way sparrows stop when a hawk goes over.
[14] King Mu: Up, boy. / The houses are parading their wrestlers in my yard, and the man they’re wrestling for is in a hedge with a jar. / Over the mountains, Silla crowned a woman this spring. Even she gets up before noon.
[15] King Euija: Let Silla crown a heifer, Father. It still owes us a river. Ha! / Meanwhile I’m practising. A crown prince ought to hit what he aims at.
[16] King Mu: Then aim at the hall. / Analects by heart at seven. My ministers beaten at go at twelve. / And twenty years since, making very sure nobody asks you to do either again.
[17] King Euija: Cleverness is an ox, Father. / Let the village see it, and by morning somebody’s hitched it to his plough.
[18] King Mu: Today it gets hitched. / Bring the jar. You’ll want it.
[19] ── SCENE: The Yard ──
[20] ¶ Five days before a crown prince is made, each of the eight houses brings a boy to the palace yard to be looked at, the way you bring a horse to market. On the day itself they wrestle. The crown prince puts up a boy too.
[21] ¶ Eight boys in white stand on the sand. The ninth place is empty, and everyone is looking at it.
[22] King Mu: Your man for the sand. / Pick a son. Yung’s big enough to fall on somebody.
[23] ¶ His sons grow up already spoken for. Yung wears a Satek ring. Hyo has a Yunbi tutor. Little Pung has lovely handwriting and a Jinmo grandmother.
[24] King Euija: Put one of mine on the sand and I’m only telling the yard which house I’ve lost him to.
[25] King Mu: Then find someone who isn’t anybody’s. / Five days. After that I pick for you, and you’ll hate who I pick.
[26] ¶ Two old men reach the prince before the king has finished speaking.
[27] King Mu: Lord Yunbi… an honour to— / Lord Satek… a new—
[28] Elder Satek: Highness. The tide is with you this week. / Up and down the river they say it. Filial to his father, kind to his brothers. The Zengzi of the East of the Sea.
[29] Elder Yunbi: We said it first. On the coast road, into a headwind. / Satek heard it from us. He usually does. Through a floorboard.
[30] Elder Satek: Floorboards are cheap in Yunbi. / Everything is.
[31] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, accession notice; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 380 · cf. Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Baekje): He served his parents with filial piety and treated his brothers with fraternal love; in his time he was called the Zengzi of the East of the Sea.❞
[32] ¶ The Zengzi of the East of the Sea was cheating at go an hour ago. He smiles at both of them like a man being sold his own horse.
[33] ¶ When they have bowed themselves away, he says what he thinks. His father has been trying to cure him of that for thirty-two years.
[34] King Euija: Father… I have no interest in these clan quarrels. / A king should be for the country—
[35] King Mu: My child… learn their names anyway. / …I did not like mine either. I still say them first.
[36] King Mu: You think I like them? I’ve buried three Satek elders, and I’d dance at a fourth. / But a king rules the country he has, boy. Not the one he wants. / Fifteen sons—
[37] King Euija: Sixteen by spring. / The lady of the Hae house says it’s twins.
[38] King Mu: …Gods help the Hae. / Every son is a door, boy, and some house will try to walk through each one. / Be a father to the boys. Be a king to the doors.
[39] ── SCENE: The White River ──
[40] ¶ That night Euija sneaks out of the palace in a grey hood and a grey robe. He tells himself it is to see how the common people live. Mostly it is to get away from a list with an empty ninth line.
[41] [PLACE baekgang: Wide, slow, and fought over one berth at a time.]
[42] ¶ On the landing a Jinmo boy is shouting at four porters and a great gilt-bronze incense burner. The burner is wrapped in silk for the crown prince’s day. It is as tall as a child, with mountains on the lid, musicians on the mountains, and a phoenix on top who looks as if he would rather be elsewhere.
[43] ¶ A barefoot boy with a basket of eels comes round the stack at a run. The Jinmo boy steps back into him. The burner goes over the rail. It does not float.
[44] The Jinmo Boy: Do you know what that WAS? / My grandfather had it cast! It’s for the crown prince! It’s for the YARD—
[45] The Jinmo Boy: Do you know who my father is, you little peasant twat?
[46] Gyebek: No.
[47] The Jinmo Boy: Jinmo. JINMO. / My father sits on the rock. I can have you thrown in after it, and nobody will even write it down.
[48] ¶ Nobody on the landing moves. The porters find their feet very interesting.
[49] Gyebek: I will get it back.
[50] The Jinmo Boy: …You? / Fine. Five days. If it isn’t on my doorstep in five days, I’ll have you killed in front of the whole street.
[51] Gyebek: Five days.
[52] ── SCENE: The Diving Boy ──
[53] ¶ There is an old willow on the bank with a rock wedged in its roots. Gyebek ties one end of a rope round the rock and the other round his ankle, so the river can’t keep him. Then he goes in.
[54] ¶ The boy is going back into the water. He has been at it since morning, and he is not a strong swimmer.
[55] 🗣: That’s the eel boy. Been going in since dawn. / For the Jinmo pot? That’s down with the catfish by now. / Hey, look at that idiot! Jumping into the freezing river, haha! / Give it a day. The river’s got all the time in the world.
[56] ¶ On the second day a man in a grey hood stops at the back of the crowd. He stays longer than he means to.
[57] King Euija: What’s he after down there?
[58] 🗣: The Jinmo pot. Five days, or they kill him.
[59] King Euija: Then why hasn’t he run?
[60] 🗣: Ask him yourself. He doesn’t talk.
[61] ¶ In the palace, the crown prince has been missing for two days. King Mu has the city turned over, and says several things about his son that the herald is asked not to write down.
[62] King Mu: Start with the wine houses. / Then the other houses.
[63] The Herald: The other— ah. / Yes, Majesty.
[64] ¶ Gyebek does not eat. Nobody sees him sleep. Each time he comes up, the rock in the willow roots has shifted a finger’s width, and he reties the knot and goes back down.
[65] ── SCENE: Night on the Bank ──
[66] ¶ On the third night the crowd has gone home. Euija comes down the bank with rice balls in a leaf and a jar he has not opened, which for him is a sacrifice.
[67] King Euija: How many times have you gone in?
[68] Gyebek: Nineteen.
[69] King Euija: …You were counting?
[70] Gyebek: At twenty I would not come back out. That is why I count.
[71] King Euija: Eat. / Then tell me. Why do you do all of this?
[72] Gyebek: I gave my word.
[73] King Euija: To a Jinmo brat who’ll have you killed either way? Ha! / Run. Tonight. There’s nothing for you in Sabi. There’s nothing for you in all of Baekje. / Nobody here will even notice you’ve gone.
[74] Gyebek: I gave my word.
[75] ¶ He says it in exactly the same words, the way you set a stone back where it was.
[76] King Euija: A fine young man… what is your name?
[77] Gyebek: I have… no name.
[78] King Euija: …What? You think it makes sense to have no name, here in Baekje?
[79] ¶ Gyebek does not answer. He goes back in. Far down, in the black, something catches the moon: a curve of gold.
[80] ¶ Then the rock comes out of the willow roots. The willow, which has been leaning on that rock for a hundred years, comes after it. The rope goes taut, and the river takes the boy, the rock and the tree down together.
[81] King Euija: Hey— HEY—!
[82] ¶ The crown prince of Baekje goes in after him in a grey robe, with a knife in his teeth. He finds the rope by feel and cuts it.
[83] ¶ They come up onto the mud together and lie there like two fish.
[84] Gyebek: …Thank you.
[85] ¶ Then he gets up, picks up the cut end of the rope, and starts looking for another rock.
[86] King Euija: **Are you insane?! In that much of a hurry to stand before Yumla?!**
[87] ¶ Euija hits him once, properly, in a way princes are not taught. Gyebek goes down on the mud and stays there.
[88] ¶ He lies with his eyes open, and the tears just come, without a sound, the way the river does.
[89] ¶ It takes a while to get it out of him.
[90] ▼ FLASHBACK  No name
    [90.0] ¶ The houses go first. Silk burns faster than timber. He is still wearing the clothes they dressed him in for the morning meal.
    [90.1] ¶ Men come over the wall with torches and a list. Every name on the list is his family’s.
    [90.2] 👨: Run away… forget me, forget all of this! / Your name too. Forget it. The name is what they are hunting.
    [90.3] ¶ They tell him to run and not say the name. He says it once, into his sleeve, and then he does not.
    [90.4] ¶ They hunt him for a season. He learns which ditches drain and which porters don’t ask questions.
    [90.5] ¶ After that he begs. The noble collar is dirty enough that nobody bows.
[90] ▲ end flashback
[91] Gyebek: No name. No house. / I have my word. / If I break it, I have nothing.
[92] ¶ Euija says nothing for a long time. All week he has been called the Zengzi of the East of the Sea by men who would sell him by the pound, and he had decided there were no honourable men left in Baekje. It is very annoying to be proved wrong about that on a mudbank, at night, by an eel boy.
[93] ¶ Before dawn Gyebek goes in one more time, with no rope at all. He reaches the gold. He gets both arms round it. Halfway up, with the surface a body’s length away, his eyes close.
[94] ¶ Under the water, there is a flash of light.
[95] ── SCENE: The Deer ──
[96] ¶ On the bank the crown prince-to-be is wearing a crown he has no business wearing. He took it out of his father’s chest that afternoon, the way he has been taking things out of his father’s chest since he was six.
[97] ¶ Out of the river, as if the water were a door, walks a pale stag with tall antlers. Across its back lies a boy with no name, both arms still locked round a gilt-bronze incense burner.
[98] ¶ Nobody else sees it. Nobody else is up.
[99] ── SCENE: The Fifth Morning ──
[100] ¶ On the fifth morning Gyebek knocks at the Jinmo gate with the incense burner on his back, wrapped in his own shirt.
[101] The Jinmo Boy: That’s— how did you— / Nobody could— it’s twenty feet of river down there—
[102] Gyebek: I said I would get it back.
[103] The Jinmo Boy: …There’s mud in the mountains.
[104] Gyebek: Yes.
[105] ── SCENE: The Sand ──
[106] ¶ The investiture takes less time than the wine did. A seal, a robe, and the whole hall bowing at once, like barley under wind.
[107] King Mu: Crown Prince. / There. Now they have to bow to you first and complain about you second.
[108] King Euija: They complained first for thirty-two years, Father. / I’ll take the bow.
[109] ¶ Then the yard. The houses’ boys stand at the edge of the sand in white. The herald reads the board.
[110] The Herald: For the house of Satek…! / For the house of Yunbi…! / For the house of Jinmo…! / And for His Highness the Crown Prince—
[111] ▼ FLASHBACK  The edict · 왕명
    [111.0] ¶ When he woke on the bank, the man in the grey hood was still wearing the crown.
    [111.1] King Euija: First, a surname. / How about… Buyeo?
    [111.2] Gyebek: Buyeo… / Is that not the royal surname? How can you…
    [111.3] ¶ Behind him, in the reeds, the deer is standing.
    [111.4] King Euija: I’ll say it again. / Do you accept my royal edict…?
    [111.5] ¶ Gyebek does not answer. He has never been given anything he did not have to pay back.
    [111.6] King Euija: Now you’ll need a name as well. / Gye, for Utmost. Bek, for Nobility. / How about — “Gyebek”? / Gyebek… a name only for men of the utmost nobility.
    [111.7] King Euija: Gyebek, would you like to serve a higher purpose?
    [111.8] Gyebek: …Do you like the name, or do you like me?
    [111.9] King Euija: …People don’t usually ask that.
    [111.10] Gyebek: I have to ask, or I do not know.
    [111.11] Gyebek: Yes.
[111] ▲ end flashback
[112] The Herald: — Buyeo Gyebek!
[113] [CARD Gyebek: A boy with no name until a prince lent him one. He means to pay it back.]
[114] [HANJA 階伯: A rung and an elder. A man with no clan, named for a ladder.]
[115] ¶ The yard says the surname back to itself, louder each time. A royal name on an eel boy. At the edge of the sand the Jinmo boy goes the colour of his burner.
[116] ▼ FLASHBACK  Five days · 닷새
    [116.0] 👨: Run away… forget me, forget all of this!
    [116.1] The Jinmo Boy: Do you know who my father is, you little peasant twat?
    [116.2] 🗣: Hey, look at that idiot! Jumping into the freezing river, haha!
    [116.3] King Euija: Why do you do all of this?
    [116.4] King Euija: Gyebek, would you like to serve a higher purpose?
[116] ▲ end flashback
[117] ¶ Gyebek looks back, and up, at the royal seats. The crown prince is already looking at him.
[118] ¶ **Eight houses. Eight boys on the sand. And one with a borrowed name…!**
